MoQueries.h:
Answer interval or tree path queries by finding an approximate TSP through the queries,
and moving from one query to the next by adding/removing points at the ends.
If values are on tree edges, change \texttt{step} to add/remove the edge $(a, c)$ and remove the initial \texttt{add} call (but keep \texttt{in}).
For range sums, let \texttt{add} increase \texttt{cur} by \texttt{a[ind]}, \texttt{del} decrease it, and \texttt{calc} return \texttt{cur}.
SuffixTree.h:
Ukkonen's algorithm for online suffix tree construction.
 Each node contains indices [l, r) into the string, and a list of child nodes.
 Suffixes are given by traversals of this tree, joining [l, r) substrings.
 The root is 0 (has l = -1, r = 0), non-existent children are -1.
 To get a complete tree, append a dummy symbol -- otherwise it may contain
 an incomplete path (still useful for substring matching, though).
Allocate the large object on the heap. The LCS helper additionally requires \texttt{ALPHA=28}.
LinearRecurrence.h:
Generates the $k$'th term of an $n$-order
linear recurrence $S[i] = \sum_j S[i-j-1]tr[j]$,
given $S[0 \ldots \ge n-1]$ and $tr[0 \ldots n-1]$.
Faster than matrix multiplication.
Useful together with Berlekamp--Massey.
Define \texttt{mod} before use; the example uses \texttt{mod=5}.
SolveLinear2.h:
To get all uniquely determined values of $x$ back from SolveLinear, make the following changes:
Define \texttt{undefined} as \texttt{numeric\_limits<double>::quiet\_NaN()} or another chosen sentinel.
NumberTheoreticTransform.h:
ntt(a) computes $\hat f(k) = \sum_x a[x] g^{xk}$ for all $k$, where $g=\text{root}^{(mod-1)/N}$.
N must be a power of 2.
Useful for convolution modulo specific nice primes of the form $2^a b+1$,
where the convolution result has size at most $2^a$. For arbitrary modulo, see FFTMod.
   \texttt{conv(a, b) = c}, where $c[x] = \sum a[i]b[x-i]$.
   For manual convolution: NTT the inputs, multiply
   pointwise, divide by n, reverse(start+1, end), NTT back.
Inputs must be in [0, mod).
Use \texttt{ModPow} with the same modulus and retain only one definition of \texttt{mod}.
ModInverse.h:
Pre-computation of modular inverses. Assumes LIM $\le$ mod and that mod is a prime.
Paste the precomputation inside a function after defining \texttt{mod} and \texttt{LIM}.
ModSqrt.h:
Tonelli-Shanks algorithm for modular square roots. Finds $x$ s.t. $x^2 = a \pmod p$ ($-x$ gives the other solution).
Use the three-argument \texttt{modpow(b, e, p)} from \texttt{ModMulLL.h} instead of the fixed-modulus dependency.
MinCostMaxFlow.h:
Min-cost max-flow.
 If costs can be negative, call setpi before maxflow, but note that negative cost cycles are not supported.
 To obtain the actual flow, look at positive values only.
Also include \texttt{bits/extc++.h} for the PBDS queue.
CentroidDecomposition.h:
Recursively find the centroid of a tree and its subtrees.
Add answer or parent bookkeeping at the marked callback.
KnuthDP.h:
When doing DP on intervals: $a[i][j] = \min_{i < k < j}(a[i][k] + a[k][j]) + f(i, j)$, where the (minimal) optimal $k$ increases with both $i$ and $j$,
 one can solve intervals in increasing order of length, and search $k = p[i][j]$ for $a[i][j]$ only between $p[i][j-1]$ and $p[i+1][j]$.
 This is known as Knuth DP. Sufficient criteria for this are if $f(b,c) \le f(a,d)$ and $f(a,c) + f(b,d) \le f(a,d) + f(b,c)$ for all $a \le b \le c \le d$.
 Consider also: LineContainer (ch. Data structures), monotone queues, ternary search.
The example evaluates a small recurrence directly; apply the optimal-split bounds above for the optimization.
DivideAndConquerDP.h:
Given $a[i] = \min_{lo(i) \le k < hi(i)}(f(i, k))$ where the (minimal)
optimal $k$ increases with $i$, computes $a[i]$ for $i = L..R-1$.
The example uses $dp[i][k]=(i-k)^2$ for $0\le k<i$; \texttt{res[i]} stores the best split and its cost.
BumpAllocatorSTL.h:
BumpAllocator for STL containers.
Keep total allocation below the shared arena size; deallocation does not reclaim space.
Timer.h:
Runs until close to the time limit. Good for brute forcing solutions.
Keep \texttt{start} and \texttt{timeLimit} outside the loop and refresh \texttt{now} inside. Print the saved answer at the marked timeout location before \texttt{exit(0)}.
GeneralMatching.h:
Matching for general graphs.
Fails with probability $N / mod$.
The returned pairs may appear in any order.
Dinic.h:
Integer max-flow and s-t min-cut; capacities are nonnegative and $s\ne t$.
The fourth \texttt{addEdge} argument is reverse capacity (default 0; use $c$ for undirected edges).
\texttt{calc} returns additional flow and updates residual capacities \texttt{c}; signed edge flow is \texttt{oc-c}.
Read the source side with \texttt{leftOfMinCut} after \texttt{calc}.
\par For bipartite matching, \texttt{g[u]} lists right IDs $[0,m)$ and \texttt{r.size()=m}.
\texttt{dfsMatching} keeps \texttt{g} unchanged, returns the size and fills \texttt{r[right]=left} ($-1$ if unmatched).
\texttt{hopcroftKarp} is an alias.
\texttt{cover(g,n,m)} returns left IDs $u$ and right IDs $n+v$; its complement is a maximum independent set.
Zfunc.h:
\texttt{z[i]} is the LCP of \texttt{s[i:]} and \texttt{s}, except \texttt{z[0]=0}.
For extended KMP, run Z on pattern + separator + text; choose a separator absent from both.
Then \texttt{z[pattern.size()+1+i]} is the LCP of the pattern and the text suffix at $i$.
